observations.finding: 0/50 Hallmark pathways significant at q<0.05 (min q=0.170); top effects include hypoxia (-1.05), spermatogenesis (+1.04), interferon gamma (-0.86), IL6/JAK/STAT3 (-0.85), interferon alpha (-0.84) down.

2/22 genes significant at q<0.05; VHL strongly depleted (12.5% vs 62.1%, OR 0.087, 95% CI 0.019-0.409, q=0.0042) and PBRM1 depleted (0% vs 44.8%, OR 0.037, 95% CI 0.002-0.640, q=0.0042). MUC16 enriched (25% vs 4.6%, OR 6.92, q=0.140) and TP53 enriched (12.5% vs 1.1%, OR 12.3, q=0.342) not significant after adjustment.

2/49 continuous features significant (min q=0.0117); chr9q (+0.63) and JAK2 (+0.56) higher in set. Gain/loss: 1 feature significant; chr1p loss enriched (31.3% vs 2.3%, OR 19.3, q=0.045). SETD2, PBRM1, BAP1, VHL loss depleted (62.5% vs 86-90%) not significant after adjustment.

reports.statistical_interpretation: RNA shows no significant pathways but large effect sizes in a coherent direction (hypoxia, interferon, IL6 down). WXS shows strong, significant depletion of VHL and PBRM1. CNV shows significant chr9q/JAK2 elevation and chr1p loss enrichment, with coherent depletion of VHL/PBRM1/SETD2/BAP1 losses.
reports.medical_interpretation: C0004 exhibits a distinct molecular profile characterized by significant VHL and PBRM1 mutation depletion, chr9q/JAK2 copy-number elevation, chr1p loss enrichment, and a coherent (though nonsignificant) transcriptional pattern. This constitutes meaningful biological evidence for set identity, with WXS and CNV providing the strongest signals.
limitations: RNA pathway findings not significant after adjustment.
